cases.customer_question: How can a Bluetooth SIG registration be completed when included QDIDs cause ICS inter-layer dependency invalid errors due to unsupported GAP or LL features?
question_variants: How do I fix GAP inter-layer inconsistency errors during product registration?
What should be done when included QDIDs generate Invalid ICS dependency errors?
Can a Subset QDID be created to resolve ICS consistency check failures?
How do I avoid additional testing caused by changing ICS values manually?
What is the correct way to handle unsupported GAP or LL features in reused QDIDs?
cases.actual_issue: The included QDIDs contained ICS settings that conflicted with the target product's supported feature set, causing inter-layer dependency validation errors during Bluetooth SIG registration. Manually correcting the ICS values in the product registration triggered generation of additional mandatory test items and required new test reports.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The reused Bluetooth qualification designs included features marked as supported even though the target product did not support them. The Bluetooth SIG consistency checks detected the mismatch and blocked normal registration. Instead of manually changing the ICS values in the registration, the consultant recommended having the original Listing Owner create official Subset QDIDs with the unsupported features disabled.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant explained that the registration failures were caused by inter-layer dependency checks tied to GAP and LL ICS items. Specifically, reused QDIDs marked certain GAP and LL features as supported even though dependent lower-layer features were not supported, causing Invalid consistency errors. The consultant warned that manually changing the ICS values in the registration workspace would cause all test cases linked to those ICS items to appear in the Test Plan, requiring additional testing and upload of new test reports. To avoid unnecessary retesting, the consultant recommended requesting that the Listing Owners create official Subset Designs changing the relevant ICS items from YES to NO. The consultant also clarified that creating the Subset itself would not incur SIG fees.
cases.decision_logic: Bluetooth SIG inter-layer dependency validation checks require consistency between supported features across protocol layers. Manually overriding ICS values in a reused design effectively creates a modified design, which triggers additional qualification test requirements. An officially created Subset QDID preserves reuse eligibility while aligning the ICS declarations with the actual supported feature set.
cases.final_recommendation: Request the original Listing Owners to create official Subset QDIDs that change the affected ICS items from YES to NO, then use those Subset QDIDs in the new product registration instead of manually modifying ICS values in the workspace.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: If the ICS values are manually modified instead of using an official Subset QDID, the Qualification Workspace may generate extensive additional test requirements and require new test reports, increasing qualification effort, delays, and risk of inconsistent registration evidence.
